channel.title: Financialist News
channel.description: Daily money news from Financialist: debt relief, consumer rights, insurance, banking and your money.

item.title: Credit Counseling vs. Debt Settlement vs. Credit Repair: The CFPB’s Differences
item.description: Counselors are usually nonprofits. Settlement and repair companies are typically for-profit and charge for steps you can take yourself for free.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Charged an Overdraft Fee? Opt-In Rules for Debit Cards, and Where They Do Not Apply
item.description: Banks cannot charge overdraft fees on one-time debit and ATM transactions unless you opted in, but checks and recurring payments are different.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: What Happens If Your Car Is Repossessed? Your Rights, Per the CFPB
item.description: Notice rules vary by state. Lenders may not “breach the peace,” and a repossession can stay on your credit reports for up to seven years.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Medical Bill Sent to Collections? What the CFPB Says About Surprise-Bill Limits and Credit Reporting
item.description: Collecting or reporting amounts above what the No Surprises Act permits may violate federal law. Dispute in writing as soon as possible.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: How to Dispute an Error on Your Credit Report, Step by Step (CFPB)
item.description: Dispute with the credit reporting company first, then with the company that supplied the information. Furnishers generally must respond within 30 days.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Can a Debt Collector Garnish Your Wages or Benefits? What the CFPB Says
item.description: Most creditors need a court judgment first. Banks must protect two months of directly deposited federal benefits.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Sued by a Debt Collector? Why Responding Matters, Per the CFPB
item.description: If you do not respond by the date in the court papers, a default judgment can follow, opening the door to garnishment, liens and frozen accounts.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Can Collectors Chase a Debt That Is Several Years Old? What the CFPB Says About Time Limits
item.description: Debts do not generally expire, but most states limit lawsuits to three to six years. A partial payment may restart the clock.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: What a Debt Validation Notice Must Include, and the 30-Day Window to Dispute
item.description: The CFPB lists the information a collector generally must send, and says a written dispute inside 30 days pauses collection until they respond.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: What to Do When a Debt Collector Contacts You, According to the CFPB
item.description: Collectors generally must give validation information within five days of first contact. Ignoring a valid debt usually will not make it go away.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Michigan Unemployment Agency Warns: It Never Charges a Fee to Release Benefits
item.description: The UIA’s Cybersecurity Awareness Month tips cover fake calls, texts and emails, password hygiene and where to report unemployment fraud.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: IRS Tax Relief for Indiana Storm and Flood Victims: Deadlines Postponed to Feb. 1, 2027
item.description: The IRS news release was updated October 8 to add more counties. Late penalties in the postponement period can be abated by calling the notice number.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Minnesota AG Tells Regulators Utility Affordability Means Paying Bills Without Sacrificing Health, Safety or Dignity
item.description: Keith Ellison spoke at the Public Utilities Commission’s first session in a statewide investigation of electric and gas affordability.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: North Carolina AG Launches Fuel Check as State Gas Tax Is Suspended Through Nov. 30
item.description: Drivers can report stations that do not pass along the 41-cent-per-gallon savings at ncdoj.gov/ncfuelcheck or 1-877-5-NO-SCAM.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC Alert: Sextortion “Help” Services Charged Thousands and Did Not Deliver, Agency Alleges
item.description: The FTC’s consumer alert names Digital Forensics and lists free steps for victims, including the 48-hour Take It Down rule.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Can’t Afford Your Student Loan Payment? What Federal Student Aid Says About Deferment and Forbearance
item.description: The agency says to contact your servicer, but warns that interest can still accrue and discharge progress can be affected.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: How Federal Student Loan Payments Are Calculated Under IBR, PAYE, RAP and Standard Plans
item.description: Federal Student Aid lists the payment formula and repayment period for each plan open to former SAVE borrowers.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SAVE Plan Borrowers Have 90 Days to Pick a New Repayment Plan, Federal Student Aid Says
item.description: Servicers began sending notices July 1, 2026. Borrowers who miss the final 30-day notice are placed in a fixed payment plan.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: DOJ: Actions Against North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More Than 70 U.S. Companies
item.description: Prosecutors announced an indictment, two arrests and the seizure of about 187 computers from suspected laptop farms in Texas.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC and States Ask Court to Hold Martin Shkreli in Contempt of Industry Ban
item.description: The coalition alleges he traded and commented on pharma stocks in violation of a 2022 order that also required $64 million in disgorgement.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Pennsylvania AG Charges Ex-Adjuster in $949,639 Fake Accident Claim Scheme
item.description: Prosecutors say Glenn Allen Johnson set up a sham law firm and used his insurer job to approve a payment to it.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Michigan Regulators Share Tips to Avoid Scams During Medicare Open Enrollment
item.description: Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7. Officials say never give your Medicare number to unsolicited callers and call 1-800-MEDICARE to verify.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Wagner Equipment to Pay $200,000 to Settle EEOC Disability and Retaliation Suit
item.description: The EEOC says the company required a 100-pound lift test that did not match the job and refused to let an employee return from medical leave.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Il Fornaio to Pay $3 Million to Settle EEOC Sexual Harassment Suit
item.description: The EEOC says at least 100 women, many of them teenagers, were affected across the chain’s California and Nevada restaurants.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: OFAC Settles With Freight Forwarder Pegasus Worldwide Logistics for $175,015
item.description: Treasury says Pegasus dealt in blocked property and took six months to fully answer an OFAC subpoena. OFAC called the conduct non-egregious.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Tennessee Joins 45-State Generic Drug Settlements With Ascend, Citron and Mayne
item.description: Ascend would pay $400,000 and Mayne $650,000. The states’ first trial is set for February 2027 in Hartford.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Pennsylvania AG Sues Insulin Makers and PBMs Over Alleged Price Manipulation
item.description: The complaint names Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Sanofi, Express Scripts, CVS Caremark and Optum Rx. It seeks restitution for Pennsylvanians.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Laundering Proceeds of $6 Million Medicare Equipment Fraud
item.description: DOJ says Advanced Medical Supply billed Medicare for braces patients never ordered. Beneficiaries mailed boxes back with notes calling it a scam.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: DOJ: “Joint Disruption Week” Hits West African Scam Networks, 3.7 Million Accounts Removed
item.description: Law enforcement made 28 arrests in Ghana and Nigeria. Private partners say they flagged over $11 million in potentially freezable funds.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: CVS Agrees to Pay $315 Million Over Opioid Prescriptions and False Claims, DOJ Says
item.description: The settlement covers October 2013 through December 2025. CVS must add safeguards, including monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Pennsylvania AG Settles With Mavis Tire for $215,000 Over Alleged Unnecessary Repairs
item.description: Consumers who believe they were billed for services they did not need have until January 26, 2027 to file a complaint for restitution.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: White House Says Nearly 70 Million Trump Accounts Created, Parents Must Claim Them
item.description: The administration reports $4.5 billion deposited since July 4. Family contributions are capped at $5,000 a year and employer contributions at $2,500.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC, Utah and Nevada Sue Lens.com Over Hidden “Taxes & Fees” on Contact Lenses
item.description: The complaint alleges a mandatory charge buried at checkout often doubles the advertised price. Lens.com’s AutoRefill plan is also challenged.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: DOJ Fraud Division Directive 26-13 Calls for Early Asset Seizures and Infrastructure Takedowns
item.description: Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald’s memo tells prosecutors to use tax, securities, consumer fraud and cyber authorities together.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Treasury’s OFAC Removes 125 Names From Sanctions Lists in Third Modernization Round
item.description: OFAC also updated 22 entries to improve compliance screening. Removed entries include deceased people, defunct companies and entries lacking identifying information.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: OCC Lets National Banks Close Offices in Areas Hit by Hurricane Isaias
item.description: The proclamation covers affected areas of Alabama and Mississippi. The OCC expects only directly affected offices to close and reopen quickly.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: New York AG Indicts Queens Pharmacy Owner Over Alleged $31 Million Medicaid and ADAP Fraud
item.description: Letitia James says Miguel Baron paid cash kickbacks and billed for medications never dispensed. A civil forfeiture action seeks over $95 million.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: CMS Publishes 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Star Ratings Ahead of Open Enrollment
item.description: CMS says about 37% of MA-PD contracts earned four stars or higher. Open enrollment runs October 15 to December 7, 2026.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FDA Updates Salmonella Outbreak Investigation Tied to Recalled Broccoli Sprouting Seeds
item.description: The FDA says not to use recalled lots from Gardeners Basics, Eden Brothers and Home Grown. The investigation is ongoing.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Iowa Unclaimed Property Program Passes $450 Million Returned
item.description: State Treasurer Roby Smith says the program returned a record $38.2 million in fiscal 2026. A new Money Match tool returns some property without a claim.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Pacearth Recalls About 110,550 Swing Seats Sold on Amazon After Fall Injuries
item.description: CPSC says seats, carabiners or straps can break. Pacearth has received at least 30 fall reports with nine injuries, and offers a full refund.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC Warns 24 Large Healthcare Companies That Hidden Prices Can Be Deceptive
item.description: Chairman Andrew Ferguson’s letters say meeting CMS price transparency rules does not create a safe harbor under the FTC Act.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC and USDA Seek Public Comment on Farm Equipment Markets, Comments Due December 7
item.description: The joint inquiry asks farmers and repair providers about barriers to buying and servicing agricultural equipment.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC Settles With Southern Glazer’s Over Wine and Spirits Price Discrimination
item.description: The order covers nearly all Southern sales to the five largest chain retailers in 26 states, with cash payments to small businesses if a monitor finds a violation.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Settles With Ex-GigaMedia Access CEO and Executive in $37 Million Investor Fraud Case
item.description: Robert Bernardi agreed to disgorgement of $4.7 million plus interest, deemed satisfied by criminal restitution. The SEC says Sunil Chandra posed as a customer employee.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Obtains Judgments Totaling About $5.7 Million Against Three BitConnect Promoters
item.description: Courts ordered Michael Noble, Craig Grant and Trevon Brown to pay disgorgement, interest and penalties over the BitConnect “lending program.”
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Encinitas Investment Adviser in Alleged Cherry-Picking Scheme
item.description: The SEC says Darren Caris steered profitable trades to his own account and losing trades to clients from December 2023 to April 2024.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Former Global Tech Industries CEO Over Share Issuances “For Services”
item.description: The SEC alleges David Reichman issued tens of millions of shares to family and associates who provided no services, and hid his daughter’s large holding.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Mississippi Man Over $1.94 Million in Medical Marijuana Investor Funds
item.description: The SEC alleges Thomas Moore raised about $4.94 million for Mississippi Green Oil and spent $1.94 million on personal items such as jewelry and travel.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Former Pharma HR Executive With Insider Trading Ahead of Adamas Deal
item.description: The SEC alleges Mukesh Asudani and two other accounts made about $78,751 after the Supernus-Adamas announcement. Adamas stock rose about 75%.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Florida Marketer Convicted in COVID-19 Testing Scheme That Billed Medicare Over $15 Million
item.description: Prosecutors say seniors at West Palm Beach-area clubs got tests they did not want. Medicare paid more than $500,000.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Treasury: Do Not Pay Reaches 99% of Federal Programs, $3.7 Trillion in Payments Verified
item.description: Treasury says it screened more than 1.1 billion payments in fiscal 2026 and returned about 13,500 payments totaling $175 million that were headed to deceased people.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Treasury Announces First Outbound Investment Program Penalty: $200,000 Against Amidi
item.description: Treasury says Amidi failed to notify it of a roughly $92,478 investment by a Chinese fund subsidiary in an AI robotics company.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Federal Reserve Announces Enforcement Action Against American Express Over Money Laundering Controls
item.description: The Fed cites failures to detect and report suspicious activity. The OCC issued a separate action against the company’s national bank.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Minnesota Woman Convicted in $3.6 Million Medicaid Housing Services Fraud
item.description: A federal jury found Sharmaine Meadows billed for services that were not provided. DOJ says the program shut down after costs ran 4,000 percent over estimates.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Former Nodus International Bank Chairman Sentenced to 62 Months for Looting the Bank
item.description: Juan Francisco Ramirez must forfeit about $13.6 million. DOJ says the scheme caused at least $23.6 million in losses and helped sink the Puerto Rican bank.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: New York AG Secures Up to $35 Million and Industry Ban From Ex-Celsius CEO Mashinsky
item.description: Letitia James says Alex Mashinsky misled more than 26,000 New York investors. He is permanently barred from securities, commodities and crypto.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: North Carolina Wins Default Judgment Against Wedding Photography Company
item.description: The court ordered about $600,000 in restitution and more than $1.1 million in civil penalties. The AG says couples paid for photos and videos they never received.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Georgia AG Warns of Price Gouging and Scams Ahead of Hurricane Isaias
item.description: The state of emergency took effect October 8. Retailers may not raise prices on goods the governor designates, including motor fuel.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Nevada AG Urges Consumers to Claim Compensation for Inflated Generic Drug Prices
item.description: A federal court gave preliminary approval in late September to a plan to distribute about $96.5 million in settlement funds paid by generic drug makers.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: 43 States Seek Approval of $400 Million Sandoz Generic Drug Price-Fixing Settlement
item.description: Washington’s attorney general says a coalition filed October 1 in Connecticut federal court. Consumers who bought generics from May 2009 to December 2019 may be eligible.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Fintech Kalder and Founder Over Inflated Revenue in $6.7 Million Raise
item.description: The SEC alleges Kalder kept two sets of books and counted demo accounts as paying customers. Founder Gökçe Güven agreed to a bifurcated settlement.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges India-Based Man With Providing a Phony Audit Report to a U.S. Public Company
item.description: The SEC alleges Himanshu Jindal posed as a U.S. CPA and forged an engagement letter. The false report went into a Form 10-K that investors relied on.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Ex-Western Asset CIO Ken Leech, $103 Million for Investors
item.description: Leech would pay a $3 million penalty and face an officer-and-director bar. With Western Asset’s $100 million penalty, the SEC says $103 million goes to harmed investors.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC Closes Gildan and S&S Probe After Contract Change on Wholesale T-Shirt Pricing
item.description: The FTC says the partners amended an agreement that barred Gildan from offering S&S-level pricing to rival distributors. It cites the Robinson-Patman Act.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC: Premier Martial Arts Franchisor and Sales Firm to Pay $1.85 Million
item.description: The FTC says deceptive earnings claims drew more than 200 buyers to $49,500 franchises. Some franchisees would get the option to cancel without penalty.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Charges Two Former Linqto Executives Over Pre-IPO Share Sales
item.description: The SEC says a Linqto subsidiary sold more than $430 million of pre-IPO vehicles to retail investors. It alleges prices were above fair value and “sold out” claims were false.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC: SQN Capital and CEO Settle Charges, Receiver Appointed for Four Funds
item.description: The SEC says the New York adviser inflated fund values and missed audits for years. Jeremiah Silkowski agreed to a $200,000 penalty and an adviser bar.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Wins Final Judgments in Boiler-Room Microcap Stock Fraud Case
item.description: The SEC says a call center pushed 18 small-company stocks and generated more than $58 million in trading proceeds. Raymond Dove must pay about $4.6 million after a default judgment.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Texas Ponzi Case: Two Men Agree to Final Judgments in $91 Million Scheme
item.description: The SEC says the "Vanguard JV Cash Program" raised at least $91 million from more than 200 investors. Conner must pay about $10.4 million and Welsh about $1.7 million.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SEC Says California Adviser Gave Himself the Winning Trades and Clients the Losers
item.description: The SEC charged Darren Caris and his firm over alleged "cherry-picking" from December 2023 to April 2024. The allegations are unproven.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Gardeners Basics Recalls Broccoli Sprouting Seeds Over Possible Salmonella
item.description: The one-pound bags sold on Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop, eBay and Etsy. Throw them out; no return is required.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: The Conqueror Recalls Avengers Infinity Gauntlet Medals Over Loose Magnets
item.description: About 476 medals sold in March to May 2026 for about $50. Choose a refund or a replacement.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Giant Recalls LED-Light Keys on SureLock Bike Locks Over Button Battery Risk
item.description: The keys do not meet the federal button battery standard. The refund is $5, and the lock itself stays usable.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Van Rysel GRVL AF Bikes Recalled Because the Front Wheel Can Come Loose
item.description: About 1,150 gravel bikes. The free repair is done at REI Co-op stores.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: DR Power Recalls 42,860 Trimmer Mowers After 19 Fire Reports; Repair Is Free
item.description: CPSC says grass and debris can build up and ignite. Two minor injuries were reported.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Snow Peak Recalls Takibi Propane Inserts: Lava Rocks Can Explode When Heated
item.description: About 100 units sold for about $350. Owners can get a refund, or keep the insert and get replacement rocks.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Romorgniz Six-Drawer Dressers Recalled: 12,078 Sold on Amazon, Refund Available
item.description: CPSC says unanchored dressers can tip over and violate the STURDY Act standard. No injuries were reported.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: ONTHEWEI Baby Bath Seats Recalled: Stop Using Them and Ask for a Refund
item.description: CPSC says the seats can tip over and violate the federal bath seat standard. About 2,140 were sold on Amazon.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Texas Roofing Company Ordered to Pay $1.5 Million; Victims Can Get Restitution
item.description: The judgment finds 27 deceptive-practice violations and sets aside at least $500,000 for victims.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Generic Drug Price-Fixing: New Yorkers Have Until March 8, 2027 to Claim
item.description: Ascend and Mayne will pay $400,000 and $650,000. Buyers of listed generics from May 2009 to December 2019 may qualify.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Greenway Auto Group Must Advertise the Real Price Under FTC Settlement
item.description: The FTC says Greenway charged an average of more than $3,350 over the advertised price in over 92% of sales.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Cleo AI Customers: FTC Will Pay 2.1 Million People Through PayPal Starting Oct. 27
item.description: The FTC says $15.8 million goes to customers who paid for instant cash advances. Eligibility emails go out by Oct. 26.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Michigan Customers: Coinbase Will Stop Sports Event Contracts and Close Positions by Oct. 10
item.description: The state gaming board says the deal follows similar agreements with Robinhood and Kalshi. Coinbase's appeal continues.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Arizona Attorney General Appeals Rate Hikes That Nearly Doubled a Robson Ranch Water Bill
item.description: The average combined water and sewer bill went from $72.01 to $143.59 after a March approval. The state asks the court to send it back.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Colorado Indictment: Fake IDs Used to Drain Home Equity Lines at Seven Banks
item.description: Prosecutors allege more than $800,000 in losses. Both defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: FTC Explains What Parents Can Do When an Explicit Image of Their Child Is Shared Online
item.description: The consumer alert covers reporting to police and NCMEC, platform takedown requests under the Take It Down Act, and the 48-hour window.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Sentencing Shows How a Thief Tried to Take a Deceased Seattle Resident's Home and Accounts
item.description: A forged power of attorney, bank logins and brokerage takeovers were stopped by a niece and fraud restrictions.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: West Virginia: FEMA Individual Assistance Approved for Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha Counties
item.description: Residents hit by the Aug. 14-18 storms can apply online or by phone. FEMA kept its denial for Boone and Logan counties.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: Texas Attorney General Opens Investigation Into Kids' Underwear Makers Over Chemicals
item.description: Civil investigative demands went to Hanes and Fruit of the Loom. The release does not report any finding of harm.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: SSI Recipients: Report Changes by the 10th of the Month to Avoid Overpayments
item.description: Social Security's Oct. 7 notice lists what must be reported and the five ways to report wages.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.title: One Lot of Babies' Magic Tea Gripe Water Recalled After FDA Finds Undeclared Alcohols

item.title: Eden Brothers Recalls Calabrese Broccoli Seeds Over Possible Salmonella

item.description: The attorney general alleges deceptive marketing under state consumer law and seeks civil penalties. The company's response was not in the release.

item.description: The department also says its life insurance locator matched more than $35 million in coverage.
item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.author: Kseniya Dzigava

item.description: The Oct. 5 list covers ratings the FDIC assigned in July 2026 to state nonmember banks.

item.description: The IRS says its whistleblower office helped HMRC set up a rewards scheme aimed at serious tax evasion by the wealthiest.

item.description: The list includes mattresses that fail flammability rules and 17 items for infants and children.

item.description: The order covers sales to five large chains in 26 states and lasts six years under an independent monitor.

item.description: A joint bulletin for World Investor Week urges caution about rising investment fraud.

item.description: An Oct. 7 IRS tax tip lists what the right to a fair and just tax system means for people who owe.
